# tests/perf-write-results.txt — write-path benchmark record
#
# Generated by tests/perf-write.sh (run inside the VM, as root; see the
# script header for the workload definitions).  Each run appends a dated
# block; the MiB/s numbers and the briefs/ext4 ratio are the regression
# gate for the write-performance campaign.  When adding numbers for a
# perf change, record the commit the module was built at and the
# before/after numbers side by side.
#
# Workloads: seq_buffered (dd + sync), seq_fsync (fsync per 1 MiB
# record), seq_osync (O_SYNC per 1 MiB record), ld_shape (500 x 1 MiB
# files, fsync each), ld_readback (re-read the 500 files).

# --- Baseline, 2026-09-17: module built from the briefs repo tree at
# 8db3690 (i.e. kernel write path unchanged since the iomap migration).
# VM 6.12.101-lockdep, /dev/vdc1 (virtio, 100 GB), 10 GiB, 1 MiB
# records, page cache dropped before each workload.
#
# workload      briefs MiB/s   ext4 MiB/s   ratio
# seq_buffered   1157.7          554.5       2.09
# seq_fsync        59.2           66.3       0.89   <-- the one below
# seq_osync        57.4           37.5       1.53
# ld_shape         52.0           36.2       1.44
# ld_readback    1736.1         1488.1       1.17
#
# Counter evidence (briefs -o debug): seq_buffered lands 10243 journal
# records for 10240 extents with just 3 checkpoints (the buffered path
# amortizes well), but seq_fsync fires 10236 journal_checkpoints for
# 10240 fsyncs — a full ring retire per fsync — and every fsync also
# drains the inode's whole extent tree (10240 extents by the end of
# the run) and syncs all owned metadata.  The fsync path is where P1
# (per-inode dirty-node tracking) and P2 (batched commit syncs) aim.

== done 2026-09-17T07:29:47Z
# --- P1 (per-inode dirty-node tracking), 2026-09-17: module built from the
# working tree at P1 (this commit; baseline 875ec08). Same VM/device/size.
#
# briefs MiB/s     baseline    P1       delta      note
# seq_buffered      1157.7   1308.8    +13.1%   the O(E)-walk win
# seq_fsync           59.2     57.9     -2.2%   noise; per-fsync checkpoint
#                                             (10236 for 10240 fsyncs,
#                                             unchanged) dominates -- P2
# seq_osync           57.4     56.9     -0.9%   noise, same as fsync
# ld_shape            52.0     50.2     -3.5%   noise
# ld_readback       1736.1   1805.1     +4.0%
#
# The pre-snapshot drain no longer sb_breads every node in the tree per
# JRN_INODE_FULL record; it touches exactly the nodes dirtied since the
# last drain (an empty set is a no-op). seq_buffered, which journals a
# snapshot per persist, gained the predicted ~13%; the fsync-shaped
# workloads did not move because their cost is the per-fsync checkpoint
# (whole-FS owned-buffer flush + allocator bitmap sync + superblock
# commit), not the walk. That is the P2 target.
#
# Data-quality note: ext4's numbers swing run-to-run on this VM (osync
# 37.5 -> 64.2, ld_shape 36.2 -> 63.0 MiB/s between the baseline and this
# run), so the briefs/ext4 ratio is per-run context only; the
# briefs-vs-briefs columns above are the regression gate.

# --- P2 (batched commit-path metadata syncs), 2026-09-17: module built from
# the working tree at P2 (briefs_meta_batch in briefs.h converts
# briefs_journal_flush_owned PASS 2, the journal-range sync loop, and
# briefs_alloc_sync's changed-block writes to submit-all-then-wait-all,
# 64-buffer windows, plugged). Same VM/device/size. Raw run: 08:56:13Z.
#
# briefs MiB/s     baseline    P1       P2      delta vs P1   note
# seq_buffered      1157.7   1308.8   1254.1     -4.2%       noise (P1's win
#                                                        over baseline +8.3%
#                                                        still stands)
# seq_fsync           59.2     57.9     59.5      +2.8%       10236 checkpoints
#                                                        for 10240 fsyncs,
#                                                        unchanged; batching
#                                                        is working but the
#                                                        metadata round trips
#                                                        were a small slice
#                                                        of per-fsync time
# seq_osync           57.4     56.9     58.6      +3.0%
# ld_shape            52.0     50.2     54.2      +8.0%       most owned buffers
#                                                        per checkpoint of
#                                                        the shapes (500
#                                                        files), most to gain
#                                                        from one wait
# ld_readback       1736.1   1805.1   1428.6    -20.9%       read path
#                                                        untouched; 0.28-0.36s
#                                                        samples, high variance
#
# ext4 (this run): buffered 550.9, fsync 66.2, osync 67.6, ld_shape 62.0.
# Briefs/ext4 ratios are essentially unchanged from P1 (fsync 0.90x vs
# 0.90x, buffered 2.28x vs 2.29x): the batching did not shift the device
# side of the ratio, i.e. per-fsync time on this device is dominated by
# the 1 MiB data write plus the fixed whole-FS checkpoint costs (journal
# range, superboard commit, allocator scan), not by the serial metadata
# buffer waits P2 removed. The measured briefs-vs-briefs gains are real
# but modest. The remaining ~10% fsync-shape gap to ext4 is the
# structural per-fsync whole-FS checkpoint (narrowed per-inode commit
# semantics), which is explicitly deferred as a journal redesign.
